title: Security incidents and logs: NIS2 incident handling and reporting, and personal-data breaches
summary: What an organisation records so that, after a security incident, it can show which logs existed before the incident, what it knew and when, what it did, and what it reported to whom.

articles.asks: Essential and important entities take appropriate and proportionate technical, operational and organisational measures to manage the risks posed to the security of the network and information systems they use.
Notify the CSIRT or, where applicable, the competent authority without undue delay of any significant incident, and where appropriate the recipients of the services concerned.

For a significant incident: an early warning within 24 hours of becoming aware of it, an incident notification within 72 hours, an intermediate report on request, and a final report within one month of the incident notification.

Notify a personal data breach to the supervisory authority without undue delay and, where feasible, within 72 hours of becoming aware of it, unless it is unlikely to result in a risk to people's rights and freedoms; a later notification gives the reasons for the delay.
Document every personal data breach, comprising the facts relating to it, its effects and the remedial action taken, so the supervisory authority can verify compliance with the article.
When a breach is likely to result in a high risk to people's rights and freedoms, communicate it to the people concerned without undue delay.

kinds.title: Log segment sealed
kinds.when: Each time a segment of a system's log is closed: after a number of lines, a number of seconds, or a file rotation. The logseal tool in the recorder kit does this for you.

fields.name: source_ref
fields.description: Your reference for the system or log source, such as fw-edge-1 or auth-server.

fields.name: segment_index
fields.description: The position of this segment in its source's sequence, from 0, so a missing segment is caught.

fields.name: segment_start
fields.description: When the segment was opened, UTC.

fields.name: segment_end
fields.description: When the segment was closed, UTC.

fields.name: line_count
fields.description: How many lines the segment holds, so a shortened segment is caught.

fields.name: log_digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of the segment exactly as archived.

fields.name: log_format
fields.description: The format of the lines, such as syslog, journald-json or cloudtrail-json.

fields.name: previous_segment_record_id
fields.description: The record_id of the segment before this one, so a removed segment is caught.

kinds.title: Incident recorded at a stage
kinds.when: At each stage of a security incident: detected, assessed, contained, resolved, closed.

fields.name: incident_ref
fields.description: Your reference for the incident.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: The stage this record captures.

fields.name: significant
fields.description: Whether you consider it a significant incident under NIS2 at this stage.

fields.name: personal_data_breach
fields.description: Whether it is a personal data breach, as known at this stage.

fields.name: description
fields.description: The facts, as known at this stage. Refer to people by your own references, never by name.

fields.name: effects
fields.description: Its effects, as known at this stage.

fields.name: actions
fields.description: The remedial action taken, and what will be done to prevent recurrence.

fields.name: aware_at
fields.description: When you became aware of the incident, UTC: the reporting deadlines run from here.

fields.name: stage_at
fields.description: When this stage was reached, UTC.

fields.name: log_segment_record_ids
fields.description: The record_ids of the sealed log segments that cover the incident.

example.description: Repeated logins to the administration portal from an address outside the usual range, using a valid account, between 02:10 and 02:40 UTC.
example.effects: One administrator account used without authorisation; whether data was read is being established.
example.actions: Account disabled and its sessions revoked; credentials of all administrators rotated.

kinds.title: Report or notification sent
kinds.when: Each time something is sent about an incident: an early warning, a notification, an intermediate or final report, a breach notification, a communication to the people concerned.

fields.name: incident_ref
fields.description: Your reference for the incident.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: What was sent.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description: To whom it was sent.

fields.name: aware_at
fields.description: When you became aware of the incident, UTC, as stated in what was sent.

fields.name: submitted_at
fields.description: When it was sent, UTC.

fields.name: report_digest
fields.description: SHA-256 of what was sent, exactly as sent, so the copy you keep can be shown to be the one you sent.

fields.name: delay_reason
fields.description: Why it was sent after the deadline, if it was.

retention: Neither NIS2 nor GDPR Article 33(5) states how long to keep these records, and this pack does not decide it for you. Check the period with your competent authority or supervisory authority.
notes: The logs never leave you: the logseal tool in the recorder kit archives each segment on your own storage and sends only the digest of its record. A segment sealed before an intruder controlled the machine that writes it cannot be changed afterwards without it showing; what that machine writes once it is controlled can be forged at the source, and no seal changes that. Financial entities under DORA report ICT incidents under DORA, whose own pack covers them.
